newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's economy stronger than expected - Werner.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's economy stronger than expected - Werner.

text.p: Mexico's economy was slightly stronger than expected during the first part of the year, Deputy Finance Minister Martin Werner said on Thursday.

"We feel that the indicator of industrial activity in the month of January and preliminary data for February, as well as unemployment data for the first half of March, indicate the economy is probably performing slightly better than expected," Werner told reporters.
Werner also echoed recent comments by other Mexican officials by saying the government's official estimate of four percent economic growth this year was "conservative."
The official said inflation in Mexico during the summer months should be low by recent standards.
"We expect lower inflation rates. Probably in the summer months they will be very close to or below one percent per month," Werner said.
He added that the government's public finance figures would be published by the government on May 15.
